verdict.reasoning: This advisory is not about a callable function but about certifi's bundled CA certificate data: a TrustCor root (linked to a spyware-vendor investigation) is removed in certifi>=2022.12.07. Exploitability therefore depends on whether the application performs outbound TLS verification using certifi's default CA bundle (e.g., via `requests`/`urllib3`), not on any direct Python API call, so a symbol/name-based static search ('TrustCor', certifi imports) is structurally unable to confirm or rule this out — zero first-party imports of certifi is expected even when it is used, since it is almost always invoked indirectly as the default `ssl_ca_cert`/`where()` bundle inside HTTP client libraries. CTFd makes outbound HTTPS calls in several places (e.g., OAuth login against majorleaguecyber.org, webhook/file-download integrations) that are not shown in the retrieved snippets, so we cannot positively confirm either that outbound TLS verification occurs using certifi's default bundle, or that it doesn't. None of the retrieved application code snippets (config delete, signing/unserialize, Unlocks repr, admin reset) touch networking or certificate handling at all, giving no direct evidence either way. Given the advisory's risk requires a real-world MITM using a TrustCor-issued cert (a narrow, low-likelihood exploitation path) combined with the inability of static call-site matching to assess this data-only, transitively-used package, this sits in the 'uncertain' category per the guidance for advisories naming no reachable function where the vulnerable behavior sits deep in a relied-upon dependency chain.

GHSA-43fp-rhv2-5gv8 (CVE-2022-23491)
package: certifi
summary: Certifi removing TrustCor root certificate
affected: >=2017.11.05, <2022.12.07

GHSA-43fp-rhv2-5gv8 (certifi) details:
Certifi 2022.12.07 removes root certificates from "TrustCor" from the root store. These are in the process of being removed from Mozilla's trust store.

TrustCor's root certificates are being removed pursuant to an investigation prompted by media reporting that TrustCor's ownership also operated a business that produced spyware. Conclusions of Mozilla's investigation can be found [here](https://groups.google.com/a/mozilla.org/g/dev-security-policy/c/oxX69KFvsm4/m/yLohoVqtCgAJ).

GHSA-248v-346w-9cwc (CVE-2024-39689)
package: certifi
summary: Certifi removes GLOBALTRUST root certificate
affected: >=2021.5.30, <2024.7.4

GHSA-248v-346w-9cwc (certifi) details:
Certifi 2024.07.04 removes root certificates from "GLOBALTRUST" from the root store. These are in the process of being removed from Mozilla's trust store.

GLOBALTRUST's root certificates are being removed pursuant to an investigation which identified "long-running and unresolved compliance issues". Conclusions of Mozilla's investigation can be found [here]( https://groups.google.com/a/mozilla.org/g/dev-security-policy/c/XpknYMPO8dI).
